candidates.source_title: Man accused of murdering woman found dead in Rochdale flat pleads not guilty - Manchester Evening News
candidates.source_summary: Man accused of murdering woman found dead in Rochdale flat pleads not guilty Manchester Evening News
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A man has denied murdering a woman who was found dead in a flat in Rochdale. Kyle Howard, 26, is accused of murdering 44-year-old Keeley Aspinall, who was found in an address on the town’s Freehold estate on May 25. He pleaded not guilty to the single charge. Mr Howard, of Tweedale Street, Rochdale, is now set to go on trial in November. He was remanded in custody by Judge Suzanne Goddard KC. Click here to hear the latest from Manchester's courts in our newsletter A further pre-trial hearing was scheduled for October. The prosecution was represented by Rachel Faux, and the defence by Dan Gaskell during today's (August 19) hearing at Manchester Crown Court. Police were called to reports of a concern for a welfare at the property off Tweedale Street. Ms Aspinall, known to friends as Kiki, was pronounced dead at the scene. In a tribute released through GMP, her family said: "Gone too soon.. we can’t believe you are gone. We will always love you and miss you, love all your family xx." Paying tribute to Ms Aspinall, one friend told the Manchester Evening News she was 'like a sister', adding: "She was the best friend anyone could ask for. I'm going to miss her so much, she will always be in my heart."

candidates.source_title: Heywood's Pride in Place scheme without chair after Brian Davies steps down - Roch Valley Radio
candidates.source_summary: Heywood's Pride in Place scheme without chair after Brian Davies steps down Roch Valley Radio
candidates.source_body_excerpt:
The former chair for Heywood's Pride in Place scheme, Brian Davies, has stepped down, leaving the scheme temporarily without a chair for the £20 million initiative.

Elsie Blundell, MP for Heywood and Middleton North commented, saying: “Brian has done a fantastic job of getting the investment plan approved by government and starting the Pride in Place scheme.  Now it has to change to a delivery phase and it is exciting that we are looking for a new chair and two new board members to strengthen the board for this next important stage.

“We know that the community wants to see Pride in Place focus on three things: crime and anti-social behaviour, transport links, and facilities for young people. That’s what local residents have told us. Now we must deliver a transformation of the town, using this money.”

The Pride in Place project is led by the local community, with board members who represent different corners of Heywood's residents, community organisations, civil society, and businesses. After producing an investment plan and securing funding from the Government, the board is entering the project delivery phase, bringing forward and developing proposals for the £20m (£2m a year, for 10 years).

Elsie added:  “This is national money which can only be spent locally, led by the community.  It means an exciting new chapter in Heywood’s future to transform the town we see around us and create new opportunities for the people who live here.”

Heywood’s Pride in Place Board are looking for a new chair to lead the board through the next stage of its work, developing, and funding projects to shape the future of the town. They are also looking for two new members to join the board.

The Chair will lead engagement and keep Pride in Place focused on delivery through relationships with key stakeholder such as the Council, Rochdale Development Agency, the NHS, Action Together, and others.  Working with board members they will be responsible for sharing information, gaining consensus, and participation from the board and the community.

Elsie has said that anyone who is interested in applying can reach out to her office for a chat by emailing her. Elsie has said “We want a strong leader who is confidently about Heywood’s future, there is so much potential here.”

The deadline is 7th September.

candidates.source_title: Strikes back on at four Greater Manchester hospitals after payment offer withdrawals, says UNISON
candidates.source_summary: Hundreds of NHS operating theatre staff at four hospitals in Greater Manchester will be back on strike for three days next week in a dispute about overtime payments, says UNISON
candidates.source_body_excerpt:
More than 350 Northern Care Alliance Foundation Trust (NCA) employees, including nurses, clinical support workers, and housekeepers at Rochdale Infirmary, Royal Oldham Hospital, Fairfield Hospital in Bury, and Salford Royal Hospital are walking out on Monday 24th, Wednesday 26th, and Friday 28th August.

UNISON says an offer to resolve the dispute was initially tabled by NCA bosses but withdrawn before discussions could take place.

The row centres on the trust's use of an outside agency (NHS Professionals (NHSP)) to manage overtime.

When covering staff shortages, staff are entitled to time-and-a-half pay. However, the union says that in some cases, staff would earn less than they would on a normal shift, with some missing out on more than £80 per shift.

Operating theatre staff were previously on picket lines at all four aforementioned sites in June.

UNISON North West regional organiser Kevin Dolan said: “Those at the top of NCA have shown a lack of leadership and made their disregard for their staff clear.

“A deal was put on the table but taken away before we had chance to talk it over. We are ready to continue negotiations, but it’s obvious NCA has no intention of resolving this.

“This isn’t complicated. Staff are simply asking for what their contract says they’re entitled to. Nothing more.”

Staff from all four sites will gather in Salford on Wednesday 26th August for a unified day of protest.

candidates.source_title: Courteeners’ Liam Fray to voice tram announcements for concerts - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_summary: Courteeners’ frontman Liam Fray will be helping tram users find their way to Wythenshawe Park this week, with the star providing on-stop announcements for a run of major concerts at the venue this weekend.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Courteeners’ frontman Liam Fray will be helping tram users find their way to Wythenshawe Park this week, with the star providing on-stop announcements for a run of major concerts at the venue this weekend. The Middleton indie-rockers are one of the big names playing at Wythenshawe Park between Friday, August 21, and Sunday, August 30, with other headliners including The Cure, Lewis Capaldi, Pulp, and The Prodigy. Fans travelling by tram will hear the frontman’s voice on each date – including special announcements for the Middleton indie-rockers show on August 29. There will be as many double trams as possible running from the city centre every seven-and-a-half minutes. Concertgoers are advised to travel on the Airport line to Moor Road tram stop, which is around a 10-minute walk from the concert entrance. There will also be dedicated shuttle buses for all five concerts, providing direct connections from Manchester city centre and East Didsbury to Wythenshawe Park. Buses from the city centre will depart from Aytoun Street, close to Manchester Piccadilly, every six minutes, while services from East Didsbury’s Parrs Wood will run every 15 minutes. Shuttle buses will also operate after each concert to help fans return to East Didsbury and the city centre. Fans can buy an event travel pass for £8 per event day, which can be used on any combination of Bee Network bus, tram or shuttle bus on the event days. This can be bought in advance on the Bee Network app. A number of regular Bee Network bus services also stop close to Wythenshawe Park, including the 41, 103, 370 and 371 on Palatine Road and 11, 248 and 249 on Altrincham Road. People intending to travel on these services should check the Bee Network app or website before travelling as some diversions will be in place on event days.

candidates.source_summary: Local families will soon benefit from a new play area at Lower Place, funded by developer contributions and additional Rochdale South Township funding
candidates.source_body_excerpt:
The new play area will include accessible play towers, swings with cradle seats, a horse springer, slide, climbing net, and a wheelchair-accessible roundabout, along with sensory and social play panels designed to support imaginative play for younger children.

It will also include colourful wet pour safety surfacing and a new tarmac path linking the existing ramp to the new equipment, making the space easier to access and enjoy.

New bench seating will provide parents and carers with a place to sit while children play.

Councillor Tricia Ayrton, Deputy Leader of the Council, and Portfolio Holder for Climate Change and Environment, said: "This new play area at Lower Place has been designed to give local children of all abilities more opportunities to play, whether on their own or with friends. We hope it will become a bright, welcoming space for families to enjoy for years to come.”

Work has already begun on the new play area, which has been designed by Kompan for children aged 1 to 12 an is expected to be completed in five weeks.

candidates.source_title: Greater Manchester to receive £17m in funding to help with the homelessness crisis
candidates.source_summary: Through a £442 million package, the North West is to receive £37m to curb rough sleeping to get people in for the winter
candidates.source_body_excerpt:
The Greater Manchester Combined Authority is to receive £16,955,174 over three years in an attempt to tackle rough sleeping in the area as part of Prime Minister Andy Burnham's national drive to end rough sleeping that totals £442 million across the country over three years, and £37 million in the North West.

The money is to create new accommodation and support that is to be rolled out across England this winter.

Alongside emergency accommodation for those who are rough sleepers, the programme will offer help with housing, health, and other needs, in an attempt to help people build a more stable future, rather than just giving people a temporary place to stay.

Accompanying this initiative, Burnham has announced that he will host a national summit in the Autumn to bring together leaders from business, finance, charities, health, faith communities, and more to ask what role each of them could play in ending rough sleeping.

Crisis, a charity for people who are homeless, suggest that preventing 40,000 people from becoming homeless could save the taxpayer close to £370 million.

PM Andy Burnham has said:  “No-one should have to bed down in a doorway or outside a station. But we’ve seen it for so long that it feels like Westminster has started to accept it.

"I won’t accept it. That’s why my first instruction as Prime Minister was to end rough sleeping. And it’s why today we’re getting started with a national drive to get everyone in for Christmas.

"We did it in the pandemic. We can do it again. But it needs all of us. Government will put the money in. But I’m asking leaders in communities and sectors across society to play their part locally too.

"Let’s get people out the cold. And let’s bring back hope."

Of the money in the initiative, £8.4 million of the new funding is going specifically to the Ending Homelessness in Communities Fund. This takes total funding allocations announced for 100 different projects to £47 million over three years.

As well as off the street provision, the funding will help local areas deliver more than 1000 settled homes over the next three years, alongside further wraparound support to help people rebuild their lives. Labour say that areas facing the greatest pressures will receive the largest share of support, with communities all across England getting support to address rough sleeping in their area.

Alongside funding allocations, the Government is publishing guidance to help local areas mobilise quickly and deliver a consistent route off the street offer this winter. The guidance will make clear the need to ensure adequate and accessible provision for women experiencing rough sleeping, recognising that women are often underrepresented in official statistics and may be at greater risk of violence, abuse, and exploitation. Guidance encourages local areas to consider single sex accommodation with specialist, intensive and trauma informed support, for victims of domestic abuse and sexual violence. This will support the government’s commitment to halve violence against women and girls in the next ten years.

This funding comes after Andy Burnham gave his first instruction to end rough sleeping across the country.

candidates.source_title: Rochdale says goodbye to ‘a force for joy’ — the one and only Jimmy Cricket - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_summary: Rochdale will have a chance to remember legendary comedian Jimmy Cricket ahead of his funeral next week.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale will have a chance to remember legendary comedian Jimmy Cricket ahead of his funeral next week. Jimmy died on August 3, aged 80, after a short illness with his family around him. Known for his clean humour, the Northern Ireland comedian became a household name in the 1970s after working the comedy club scene. Famous for his catchphrase “And there’s more”, he lived in Rochdale and was a big supporter of local charities and causes. On Thursday, August 20, his body will lie in state at St Patrick’s Catholic Church in Rochdale from 3pm to 5pm on for anyone wanting to pay their respects. His life will then be celebrated at Salford Cathedral starting with a vigil mass for the reception of the body at 7pm. It will be followed by his funeral at 1.30pm on Friday, August 21, at the cathedral, with mourners encouraged to wear bow ties which, along with his Wellington boots, became Jimmy’s trademark. Operating under a shared Rochdale AFC identity opens up new opportunities too, from commercial support and matchday promotion to community events and sponsorship, reinforcing that women's sport has a central place in the borough's sporting future. The move follows a model seen elsewhere in professional sport, where football and rugby clubs have partnered with netball organisations to boost visibility, participation and long-term sustainability. British Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood has announced plans to amend immigration laws to remove a legal barrier that prevented the Home Office from deporting Ahmed after his British citizenship was revoked. candidates.source_body_excerpt: The ominous wrecking ball looming over a 1960s housing estate in Rochdale has returned. Empty blocks on Lower Falinge were saved from the bulldozer 11 months ago following a successful legal challenge from campaigners. Now fresh demolition plans have been revealed. Rochdale Boroughwide Housing (RBH) wants to knock down seven blocks of flats containing 150 homes and replace them with 270 new homes. The vision includes a mix of flats and houses on the land between St Mary’s Gate and Sheriff Street. Click here to get the biggest stories straight to your inbox in our Daily Newsletter In order to do this the maisonette blocks known as Ollerton, Newstead, Romsey, Quinton, Ullesthorpe and Vaynor all have to go. Only the Zedburgh block, also earmarked for demolition, is lived in. Andy Roche has been in Lower Falinge since 1988. Both he and his partner are the last holdouts in the Zedburgh block. They are ‘distraught’ by the latest news. They knew this was coming though. When RBH was stopped from demolishing the blocks last year, they were told they needed to showcase what they would actually do with the land - rather than just leave it grassed over. Although a new vision has now been revealed, it doesn’t make it any easier for Andy. Andy said: “Obviously it’s extremely distressing for me because it involves being forced out of my home. I am not happy about RBH’s proposals, but I’m not sure how to put it into words. “I’m still processing it. I don't believe they have listened to the residents of the estate at all. “My partner is also distraught. We are both autistic and this eviction is making us both really ill.” So many tenants have upped sticks and moved on, but for Andy this estate has everything he wants. He has been offered multiple different housing options by RBH, but none of them have lived up to what he currently has, he claims. Last year Andy provided a tour of the estate. Walking through the maze of flats, it looked desolate The Newstead block overlooks the communal grassland, every window boarded up with plywood. This indicated the vandalism the area suffers. Andy points out how families can watch their children play on the grass outside from through their living room windows. But there are no children here anymore, and no families. RBH says the blocks are no longer fit for purpose and have lived way beyond their life span. The social housing landlord says their new plans have been informed by the consultation of local residents. The estate is a bizarre clash of old and new though. Opposite the Ollerton block, next door to Andy’s Zeburgh block - there is a brand new play park surrounded by plush new housing. This is part of the previous phases of the overarching redevelopment already carried out by RBH. They have already delivered 100 new homes in Lower Falinge after previous demolition work. The previous phases began with demolition work in 2012, a year after Lower Falinge was named the most deprived area in England for the fifth year running. The estate took another hammering in 2016 when former Prime Minister David Cameron called it a sink estate - meaning a place that suffers from severe social and economic deprivation. That upset Andy upset. Many in his shoes would think a visit from the Prime Minister would bring hope for the future. What saddens him more is seeing the blocks that used to be full of life look derelict and silent. Seeing the blocks such as Pershore and Stavordale get refurbished to avoid damp and mould problems

candidates.source_body_excerpt: The legacy of a Rochdale reformer is still being recognised in the White House after more than 160 years. John Bright was born in Greenbank in 1811. He was a Quaker, politician, statesman, social reformer and British radical. He became friends with the US President Abraham Lincoln and the pair enjoyed a special relationship of mutual respect. A chance conversation and some digging by a Rochdale Town Hall volunteer have revealed that a bust made in tribute to him is still on display at the White House today. Lincoln had a portrait of Bright on the walls of his reception room. The bust was commissioned by Manchester solicitor Thomas Blain as a gift for the president who was assassinated before it was presented to him. The bust was added to the White House collection under President Johnson. Mayoress of Rochdale Iram Faisal shared on Facebook: “Wow! What a discovery! Never in my life could I have imagined that a chance conversation with one of our town hall volunteers would lead to such an incredible piece of history. “While talking about the fascinating history of Rochdale Town Hall, the subject of John Bright came up — our very own Rochdale-born politician, cotton manufacturer, philanthropist and one of the most influential figures of the 19th century. “John Bright was a strong supporter of Abraham Lincoln and the Union during the American Civil War, and his connection with Lincoln is a remarkable part of our shared history.

candidates.source_body_excerpt:
Newport and new manager Hayden Mullins enjoyed a dream start to their League Two campaign with a 3-0 home win over newly-promoted Rochdale.

First-half goals from summer signings Kyle Cameron and Shaquille Gwengwe put the Exiles in charge at a sun-baked Rodney Parade.

Dale's return to the fourth tier went from bad to worse when left-back Bryant Bilongo was shown a second yellow card for upending Cameron Norman in the 66th minute before Yahya Bamba added County's third late on.

Ciaran Brennan and Christian Doidge were both denied by Rochdale goalkeeper Nils Ramming before Gwengwe nipped in front of the Brighton loanee to stab in a second from Biggins' cross.

Any hopes of a Rochdale fightback were ended by Bilongo's dismissal and Bamba lashed in a third in stoppage time to add to their misery.

candidates.source_title: Hayden Mullins believes Newport County can build on victory over Rochdale - South Wales Argus
candidates.source_summary: Hayden Mullins is convinced there is a lot more to come from his Newport County AFC team, despite a superb opening-day win over Rochdale.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: HAYDEN Mullins is convinced there is a lot more to come from his Newport County AFC team, despite a superb opening-day win over Rochdale. County cruised to a 3-0 victory over the newly-promoted visitors, who were already 2-0 down when they were reduced to 10 men midway through the second half. First-half goals from Kyle Cameron and Shaquille Gwengwe and a late third from Yahya Bamba secured a first three points of the League Two season and made it a near-perfect day for the Exiles at a sun-drenched Rodney Parade. Dale didn't have a shot on target all afternoon, but Mullins believes there is still room for improvement from his side. "We know that we need to make our home form really positive this season and we wanted to lay a marker down and I think we did that," said the manager. "The boys deserve massive credit because they went about their jobs really well. They've really responded to what I'm trying to put across, they believe in the work that we've been doing and they put in a real good shift. "But I think there's definitely another level. I don't think this is us. It's the first game of the [league] season and there's definitely more levels. "Our fitness can definitely come up and there were more opportunities to score as well. "I'm so pleased for the boys that got the goals - [especially] Shaq and Yahya," he added. "That will give them such a lift.
